description_full: Cal-Maine Foods, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, engages in the production, grading, packaging, marketing, and distribution of shell eggs, egg products, and prepared foods in the United Sates. It operates through Conventional Shell Eggs, Specialty Shell Eggs, and Prepared Foods segments. The company offers specialty shell eggs, including cage-free, organic, brown, free-range, and pasture-raised and nutritionally enhanced eggs, as well as conventional and co-pack shell eggs. It also provides prepared food products, such as pre-cooked egg patties, omelets, folded and scrambled egg formats, hard-cooked eggs, pancakes, waffles, and specialty wraps. The company offers its products under the Egg-Land's Best, Land O' Lakes, Farmhouse Eggs, Sunups, 4Grain, Van's, MeadowCreek Foods, and Crepini brand names. It sells its products to various customers, including national and regional grocery store chains, club stores, independent supermarkets, foodservice distributors, and egg product consumers. Cal-Maine Foods, Inc. was founded in 1957 and is headquartered in Ridgeland, Mississippi.

financial_summary: Cal-Maine Foods, Inc. is a mid-cap consumer defensive business with a $3.1B market cap on $2.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -3% over the past three years and +4% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.

Returns on capital run at 25% against a 8% cost of capital — a 17-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 21% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $329M in free cash flow — roughly 11 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.51× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.
Management returns a meaningful 7.5% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 9.9% of the shares.
